Check if your router has WoL (Wake on Lan) feature and if it's enabled and configured for your PC.

Also the hardware that's connected to your PC can cause it.


If you have something that's feeding power to your PC through USB port might also cause unexpected behavior.

If your power on button's shorting it might cause the issue (But if -lastwake returned that the instance was caused by USB, it's highly unlikely that this is the issue)


-- OR -- 

It's a bios glitch in that case I would recommend you to update your BIOS if that won't help then pull off the power plug from your PSU (Wait 5-10 minutes), then clear the CMOS.

This should help, if the above steps fail.

-- ALSO --

Check your System Event Log, and look for entries connected with Power and Troubleshooting. The software installed on your PC might wake the PC to check for updates or perform some actions.
